subject: NovaAI — performance alignment & streaming options
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novaai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T13:15:00-08:00
Subject: NovaAI — performance alignment & streaming options

Thanks again for the sync this morning — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and the proposed next steps so our teams can run targeted validation for TTFT and streaming behavior. Please call out anything I mis-captured.

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: productionize low-latency chat for NovaAI’s realtime assistant (web + mobile).
- Primary SLOs discussed:
  • Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target p50 <= 150 ms, p95 <= 350 ms for end-user requests.
  • Throughput / concurrency: steady-state ~150 concurrent sessions, burst to ~400 concurrent sessions.
  • Typical response size: ~200–350 tokens (median ~250 tokens).
- Streaming preference: Lucia indicated WebSocket for the realtime UX, but compliance team may prefer SSE in some regions.
- Critical constraints: strict p95 tail limits (UX quality), and ability to fall back to smaller chunk cadence if network conditions degrade.

Preliminary Redwood suggestions (short):
- Primary path: WebSocket streaming with small chunk cadence (20–80 tokens per chunk or ~50–150ms cadence depending on tokenization and model).
- Fallback path: SSE with explicit chunk boundaries every 150–300 tokens to reduce overhead for older clients.
- Concurrency handling: prioritize continuous batching with warm KV cache; target warm-start capacity for bursts up to 400 concurrent streams.

Experiment proposal (what we’ll benchmark)
1) Baseline (non-streaming) — 100 concurrent sessions, measure TTFT p50/p95, end-to-end response time.
2) WebSocket streaming — run at 150 and 300 concurrent sessions; measure TTFT (first chunk) p50/p95 and average chunk cadence.
3) SSE streaming — same concurrency points; measure first-chunk delivery and total completion time.
4) Chunk cadence sweep — compare chunk sizes: 16 tokens, 64 tokens, 256 tokens; measure perceived first-byte latency and total tokens/sec.

What we need from NovaAI to start
- Sample production traffic profile (attached CSV looks great): request sizes, avg tokens, client concurrency distribution.
- A test account / short-lived API key for our test harness (we’ll limit scope and run in your staging region).
- Preferable cutover windows for load testing (UTC windows and any blackout periods).

Immediate next steps
- Action: Rishi to provision a Redwood test plan and share runbook (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Action: Monica to draft detailed measurement metrics and dashboards for the pilot (ETA: Wed 02/24).
- Action: NovaAI to confirm preferred streaming mode and share staging API key (Lucia).

Attachments: I’ve attached the usage CSV you sent and a short Redwood TTFT proposal PDF with suggested default chunk cadences.

Thanks — looking forward to the engineering sync.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novaai.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T16:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: NovaAI — performance alignment & streaming options

Thanks Rishi — this matches our notes. Couple clarifications from our infra side:
- Our median response is closer to 270 tokens; the 200–350 band you noted is correct.
- Preference is WebSocket for desktop/mobile realtime UX. For EU customers we may need SSE-only clients (security/perf team).
- Concurrency profile: peak QPS translates to ~180 concurrent websocket sessions in our canopy region, with peaks up to ~420 during promotional events.

I attached an updated novaai_mvp_usage.csv with hourly distribution and a short note about our client reconnection/backoff policy.

Can you confirm whether Redwood’s warm-start strategy can maintain p95 TTFT during an unplanned 3x burst for up to 10 minutes? That will be a gating requirement for our production SLA.

Also happy to get the engineering sync scheduled. Prefer Thu 02/25 09:00 PT.

—
Lucia Gomez
Head of AI Platform | NovaAI
lucia.gomez@novaai.com

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novaai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T17:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: NovaAI — performance alignment & streaming options

Lucia — thanks for the details and the updated CSV. Short answers up front: yes — we can design the pilot to validate warm-start behavior and 3x burst tolerance; the runbook below will exercise that path explicitly.

Runbook (engineering pilot) — suggested steps- Prep: Redwood will provision a staging model instance with your staging API key and mirror the traffic distribution you provided.
- Warm-start validation: pre-warm a subset of model workers with recent prefixes and run a 10-minute 3x burst test. Metric: p95 TTFT <= 350 ms during burst; if above, we iterate on batching/kv-warm policies.
- Cadence sweep (streaming): for WebSocket and SSE, we’ll test chunking at token sizes 16 / 64 / 256 and interval targets of 50ms / 150ms / 400ms (where applicable).
- Concurrency ramp: run steady-state at 150 sessions, ramp to 400 over 3 minutes, hold for 10 mins, then cool down. Collect p50/p95/p99 TTFT and chunk delivery stats.
- Fallback logic validation: enforce simulated packet loss and client reconnections to validate graceful degradation (SSE fallback/short-chunking).

Bench metrics we’ll report back- TTFT p50/p95/p99 (first byte and first token)
- Chunk cadence (ms between chunk emissions) and average chunk token counts
- Aggregate tokens/sec and requests/sec
- Error/retry rates and observed retransmission/backoff effects

Proposed schedule- Share runbook & load script (attached) — Rishi (today EOD).
- Engineering sync — Thu 02/25 09:00 PT (Monica + Aditya + NovaAI infra).
- Pilot window — Fri 02/26 10:00–14:00 PT (tentative, we can shift).

Can Monica & Aditya confirm the sync and the pilot window? We’ll need NovaAI to provide a staging API key and an allowlist of test IPs.

Rishi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Andre Costa <andre.costa@novaai.com>

Subject: Re: NovaAI — performance alignment & streaming options

Rishi / team — quick confirmation from infra: Thu 02/25 09:00 PT works for the sync. We can provide a staging API key with scope limited to the testing project (expires in 7 days).

One ask: we typically test with two payload shapes — short (30–60 tokens) and long (350–450 tokens). Can you include both in the cadence sweep? Also please share the exact test endpoints and auth header format so our security tooling can pre-authorize.

I’ll attach the temporary key in an internal ticket and email the allowlist. Looking forward to the pilot.

—
Andre Costa
